title: Constitutional Law I
topics: Nature and forms of a constitution
Rule of law and natural justice

items.q: Writings of jurists may be defined as
o: the published opinions of scholars, which courts may consult for guidance without being bound
the guarantee against deprivation of one's possessions except for public purposes with compensation
the doctrine that an act beyond the limits of a conferred authority is void
the fair procedure that must be followed before life, liberty or property is taken away
items.s: Writings of jurists: the published opinions of scholars, which courts may consult for guidance without being bound. The other options describe Ultra vires, Right to property, Due process.

items.q: The statement “a system in which authority is shared between a central government and component units of one state” describes which of the following?
o: Exclusive legislative list
Unitary system
Derivation
Federalism
items.s: Federalism is a system in which authority is shared between a central government and component units of one state.

items.q: Nemo judex in causa sua may be defined as
o: a measure having no legal force at all, as though it had never been made
the conflict that makes a lesser rule void to the extent that it contradicts a higher one
the principle that no one may sit in judgment on a matter in which he has an interest
the method of voting in which no one can tell how another cast his vote
items.s: Nemo judex in causa sua: the principle that no one may sit in judgment on a matter in which he has an interest. The other options describe Void act, Secret ballot, Inconsistency.
items.t: Rule of law and natural justice

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Citizenship by birth.
o: the presiding officer of the lower house, chosen by its members from among themselves
a readiness by courts to intervene boldly and shape policy through their decisions
the status acquired by being born to citizen parents, or in the country in stated cases
the conflict that makes a lesser rule void to the extent that it contradicts a higher one
items.s: Citizenship by birth: the status acquired by being born to citizen parents, or in the country in stated cases. The other options describe Speaker, Inconsistency, Judicial activism.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Secret ballot?
o: the method of voting in which no one can tell how another cast his vote
a vote in favour by a number larger than the ordinary half, such as two thirds
the liberty to hold opinions and to impart them through any medium
the requirement that appointments and institutions reflect the diversity of the whole country
items.s: Secret ballot: the method of voting in which no one can tell how another cast his vote. The other options describe Freedom of expression, Special majority, Federal character.

items.q: The statement “the doctrine that an act beyond the limits of a conferred authority is void” describes which of the following?
o: Void act
Supremacy clause
Ultra vires
Inconsistency
items.s: Ultra vires is the doctrine that an act beyond the limits of a conferred authority is void.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Deprivation.
o: authority exercised at the mere will of its holder without any settled standard
the opening provision declaring the fundamental document binding on all authorities and persons
the compulsory loss of membership for stated misconduct such as treason
the principle that a unit receives a share of revenue according to what is produced within its area
items.s: Deprivation: the compulsory loss of membership for stated misconduct such as treason. The other options describe Supremacy clause, Arbitrary power, Derivation.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Federalism?
o: the freedom from arrest or detention except on grounds and by procedure allowed by law
a system in which authority is shared between a central government and component units of one state
the liberty to go anywhere within the country and to leave and re-enter it
the principle that no one may sit in judgment on a matter in which he has an interest
items.s: Federalism: a system in which authority is shared between a central government and component units of one state. The other options describe Freedom of movement, Nemo judex in causa sua, Personal liberty.

items.q: The statement “the subjects upon which both the centre and the component states may make rules” describes which of the following?
o: Concurrent legislative list
Exclusive legislative list
Confederation
Derivation
items.s: Concurrent legislative list is the subjects upon which both the centre and the component states may make rules.

items.q: Citizenship may be defined as
o: a draft measure laid before a legislature for debate and approval
the order requiring a person holding another in custody to produce him and justify the detention
a system in which authority is shared between a central government and component units of one state
the legal status of belonging to a state and enjoying its protection
items.s: Citizenship: the legal status of belonging to a state and enjoying its protection. The other options describe Habeas corpus, Federalism, Bill.

items.q: The statement “a disposition to defer to the other organs and decide only what the case requires” describes which of the following?
o: Judicial restraint
Checks and balances
Executive
Fusion of powers
items.s: Judicial restraint is a disposition to defer to the other organs and decide only what the case requires.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Right to property?
o: the published opinions of scholars, which courts may consult for guidance without being bound
the doctrine that governmental authority must be exercised within known and enforceable limits
a measure having no legal force at all, as though it had never been made
the guarantee against deprivation of one's possessions except for public purposes with compensation
items.s: Right to property: the guarantee against deprivation of one's possessions except for public purposes with compensation. The other options describe Void act, Writings of jurists, Constitutionalism.

items.q: The statement “the principle that government must act according to known rules applied equally to all” describes which of the following?
o: Presumption of innocence
Due process
Rule of law
Nemo judex in causa sua
items.s: Rule of law is the principle that government must act according to known rules applied equally to all.
items.t: Rule of law and natural justice

items.q: The statement “the subjects upon which only the central legislature may make rules” describes which of the following?
o: Federalism
Derivation
Exclusive legislative list
Unitary system
items.s: Exclusive legislative list is the subjects upon which only the central legislature may make rules.

items.q: The statement “the holding of membership of two states at the same time” describes which of the following?
o: Deprivation
Naturalisation
Citizenship by birth
Dual citizenship
items.s: Dual citizenship is the holding of membership of two states at the same time.

items.q: Which term is described by “the liberty to hold opinions and to impart them through any medium”?
o: Right to property
Freedom of association
Right to life
Freedom of expression
items.s: Freedom of expression is the liberty to hold opinions and to impart them through any medium.

items.q: Which term is described by “the formal approval by the head of state that turns a passed bill into law”?
o: Assent
Speaker
Attorney General
Override
items.s: Assent is the formal approval by the head of state that turns a passed bill into law.

items.q: Freedom from discrimination may be defined as
o: the guarantee that no one is treated worse because of ethnic group, sex, religion or birth
one that can be altered only by a special and more demanding procedure than ordinary lawmaking
a lawmaking body with two houses that must both approve a bill before it passes
the compulsory loss of membership for stated misconduct such as treason
items.s: Freedom from discrimination: the guarantee that no one is treated worse because of ethnic group, sex, religion or birth. The other options describe Bicameral legislature, Rigid constitution, Deprivation.

items.q: Attorney General may be defined as
o: the security of tenure and salary that keeps judges free of control by other organs
the chief law officer of the state, who advises government and conducts prosecutions
a draft measure laid before a legislature for debate and approval
the organ that settles disputes and applies the rules to concrete cases
items.s: Attorney General: the chief law officer of the state, who advises government and conducts prosecutions. The other options describe Independence of the judiciary, Bill, Judiciary.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Common law?
o: the body of principles developed by the English courts and received into Nigerian practice
an agreement with another state that binds the country once turned into domestic legislation
the opportunity to know the case against one and answer it before a decision is reached
the voluntary giving up of one's membership of a state
items.s: Common law: the body of principles developed by the English courts and received into Nigerian practice. The other options describe International treaty, Renunciation, Fair hearing.

items.q: Which term is described by “the method of voting in which no one can tell how another cast his vote”?
o: Citizenship
Citizenship by birth
Secret ballot
Deprivation
items.s: Secret ballot is the method of voting in which no one can tell how another cast his vote.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Veto?
o: the legal status of belonging to a state and enjoying its protection
the body of principles developed by the English courts and received into Nigerian practice
the refusal of the head of state to approve a measure passed by the legislature
a direct vote of the people upon a proposal put to them
items.s: Veto: the refusal of the head of state to approve a measure passed by the legislature. The other options describe Referendum, Common law, Citizenship.

items.q: The statement “the organ that settles disputes and applies the rules to concrete cases” describes which of the following?
o: Legislature
Delegated legislation
Judiciary
Executive
items.s: Judiciary is the organ that settles disputes and applies the rules to concrete cases.

items.q: The statement “an unwritten rule of political practice treated as binding although no court enforces it” describes which of the following?
o: Rigid constitution
Constituent power
Constitutional convention
Written constitution
items.s: Constitutional convention is an unwritten rule of political practice treated as binding although no court enforces it.
items.t: Nature and forms of a constitution

items.q: Special majority may be defined as
o: the subjects upon which only the central legislature may make rules
the status acquired by being born to citizen parents, or in the country in stated cases
the principle that both sides must be heard before a decision affecting them is taken
a vote in favour by a number larger than the ordinary half, such as two thirds
items.s: Special majority: a vote in favour by a number larger than the ordinary half, such as two thirds. The other options describe Citizenship by birth, Exclusive legislative list, Audi alteram partem.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Freedom of expression?
o: rules made by an authority to which a lawmaking body has entrusted the power to make them
the order requiring a person holding another in custody to produce him and justify the detention
the liberty to hold opinions and to impart them through any medium
the method of voting in which no one can tell how another cast his vote
items.s: Freedom of expression: the liberty to hold opinions and to impart them through any medium. The other options describe Delegated legislation, Habeas corpus, Secret ballot.

items.q: Which term is described by “the freedom from arrest or detention except on grounds and by procedure allowed by law”?
o: Freedom of association
Personal liberty
Right to property
Fundamental rights
items.s: Personal liberty is the freedom from arrest or detention except on grounds and by procedure allowed by law.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Supremacy of the constitution?
o: the principle that every other rule or act must give way to the fundamental document and be void if inconsistent
the formal approval by the head of state that turns a passed bill into law
the principle that both sides must be heard before a decision affecting them is taken
the principle that a unit receives a share of revenue according to what is produced within its area
items.s: Supremacy of the constitution: the principle that every other rule or act must give way to the fundamental document and be void if inconsistent. The other options describe Audi alteram partem, Derivation, Assent.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Checks and balances.
o: the arrangement by which each organ can restrain the others so that none dominates
the basic norm from which every other rule in a legal order is said to derive its validity
a system in which authority is shared between a central government and component units of one state
the lawful authority of a legislature to make rules upon a particular subject
items.s: Checks and balances: the arrangement by which each organ can restrain the others so that none dominates. The other options describe Grundnorm, Legislative competence, Federalism.

items.q: Which term is described by “the organ that settles disputes and applies the rules to concrete cases”?
o: Judiciary
Legislature
Checks and balances
Judicial restraint
items.s: Judiciary is the organ that settles disputes and applies the rules to concrete cases.

items.q: The statement “a measure having no legal force at all, as though it had never been made” describes which of the following?
o: Void act
Grundnorm
Ultra vires
Judicial review
items.s: Void act is a measure having no legal force at all, as though it had never been made.

items.q: Which term is described by “a measure having no legal force at all, as though it had never been made”?
o: Ultra vires
Void act
Legislative competence
Inconsistency
items.s: Void act is a measure having no legal force at all, as though it had never been made.

items.q: The statement “rules made by an authority to which a lawmaking body has entrusted the power to make them” describes which of the following?
o: Delegated legislation
Judicial restraint
Fusion of powers
Judiciary
items.s: Delegated legislation is rules made by an authority to which a lawmaking body has entrusted the power to make them.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Renunciation?
o: the voluntary giving up of one's membership of a state
the position that an accused person is treated as blameless until the accuser proves guilt
a lawmaking body consisting of only one house
the status acquired by being born to citizen parents, or in the country in stated cases
items.s: Renunciation: the voluntary giving up of one's membership of a state. The other options describe Presumption of innocence, Citizenship by birth, Unicameral legislature.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Derogation?
o: the protection of a provision by making its alteration harder than ordinary change
the lawful suspension or narrowing of guarantees during a declared emergency
the body of principles developed by the English courts and received into Nigerian practice
an unwritten rule of political practice treated as binding although no court enforces it
items.s: Derogation: the lawful suspension or narrowing of guarantees during a declared emergency. The other options describe Common law, Entrenchment, Constitutional convention.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Renunciation?
o: the power of the legislature to pass a measure despite a refusal of approval
the power of a court to examine an act of government and set it aside as unlawful
the order requiring a person holding another in custody to produce him and justify the detention
the voluntary giving up of one's membership of a state
items.s: Renunciation: the voluntary giving up of one's membership of a state. The other options describe Habeas corpus, Judicial review, Override.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Bill?
o: a loose union in which the component units keep final authority and the centre acts as their agent
the requirement that appointments and institutions reflect the diversity of the whole country
the liberty to join with others in forming groups for lawful purposes
a draft measure laid before a legislature for debate and approval
items.s: Bill: a draft measure laid before a legislature for debate and approval. The other options describe Confederation, Freedom of association, Federal character.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Grundnorm.
o: the doctrine that an act beyond the limits of a conferred authority is void
the basic norm from which every other rule in a legal order is said to derive its validity
a lawmaking body consisting of only one house
a body of rules spread across statutes, conventions and judicial decisions rather than gathered in one document
items.s: Grundnorm: the basic norm from which every other rule in a legal order is said to derive its validity. The other options describe Ultra vires, Unicameral legislature, Unwritten constitution.

items.q: The statement “a readiness by courts to intervene boldly and shape policy through their decisions” describes which of the following?
o: Judicial activism
Judicial restraint
Fusion of powers
Checks and balances
items.s: Judicial activism is a readiness by courts to intervene boldly and shape policy through their decisions.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Due process?
o: the head of the judicial arm, who presides over the highest court in the land
the fair procedure that must be followed before life, liberty or property is taken away
the qualified entitlement to vote in public elections
the power of a court to examine an act of government and set it aside as unlawful
items.s: Due process: the fair procedure that must be followed before life, liberty or property is taken away. The other options describe Judicial review, Chief Justice, Franchise.
items.t: Rule of law and natural justice

items.q: Which of the following best describes Derivation?
o: the principle that a unit receives a share of revenue according to what is produced within its area
the opening provision declaring the fundamental document binding on all authorities and persons
the order requiring a person holding another in custody to produce him and justify the detention
an agreement with another state that binds the country once turned into domestic legislation
items.s: Derivation: the principle that a unit receives a share of revenue according to what is produced within its area. The other options describe Habeas corpus, Supremacy clause, International treaty.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Concurrent legislative list.
o: the doctrine that an act beyond the limits of a conferred authority is void
a draft measure laid before a legislature for debate and approval
the subjects upon which both the centre and the component states may make rules
a body of rules spread across statutes, conventions and judicial decisions rather than gathered in one document
items.s: Concurrent legislative list: the subjects upon which both the centre and the component states may make rules. The other options describe Bill, Ultra vires, Unwritten constitution.

items.q: Which term is described by “the conflict that makes a lesser rule void to the extent that it contradicts a higher one”?
o: Legislative competence
Inconsistency
Supremacy clause
Judicial review
items.s: Inconsistency is the conflict that makes a lesser rule void to the extent that it contradicts a higher one.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Equity?
o: the body of rules, written or unwritten, that establishes the organs of a state and limits their authority
the body of principles developed to soften the harshness of the strict old rules
the principle that a unit receives a share of revenue according to what is produced within its area
the authority of a people to adopt or replace the fundamental document of their state
items.s: Equity: the body of principles developed to soften the harshness of the strict old rules. The other options describe Derivation, Constituent power, Constitution.

items.q: All of the following belong to Nature and forms of a constitution EXCEPT
o: Supremacy of the constitution
Constitution
Written constitution
Unwritten constitution
items.s: Every other option belongs to Nature and forms of a constitution. “Supremacy of the constitution” belongs to Supremacy and judicial review, not Nature and forms of a constitution.
items.t: Nature and forms of a constitution

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Nemo judex in causa sua.
o: the opportunity to know the case against one and answer it before a decision is reached
the holding of membership of two states at the same time
a loose union in which the component units keep final authority and the centre acts as their agent
the principle that no one may sit in judgment on a matter in which he has an interest
items.s: Nemo judex in causa sua: the principle that no one may sit in judgment on a matter in which he has an interest. The other options describe Fair hearing, Confederation, Dual citizenship.
items.t: Rule of law and natural justice

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Attorney General?
o: the body of rules, written or unwritten, that establishes the organs of a state and limits their authority
the chief law officer of the state, who advises government and conducts prosecutions
an enactment of the legislature stating binding rules of general application
the overlap that occurs where the same persons sit in more than one organ
items.s: Attorney General: the chief law officer of the state, who advises government and conducts prosecutions. The other options describe Constitution, Legislation, Fusion of powers.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Judicial activism?
o: the opening provision declaring the fundamental document binding on all authorities and persons
the grant of membership of a state to a foreigner who satisfies stated conditions
the division of governmental authority among three distinct organs, each with its own function
a readiness by courts to intervene boldly and shape policy through their decisions
items.s: Judicial activism: a readiness by courts to intervene boldly and shape policy through their decisions. The other options describe Supremacy clause, Separation of powers, Naturalisation.

items.q: Fair hearing may be defined as
o: the method of voting in which no one can tell how another cast his vote
the overlap that occurs where the same persons sit in more than one organ
the opportunity to know the case against one and answer it before a decision is reached
a formal change to the text of a constitution made by the procedure the document itself lays down
items.s: Fair hearing: the opportunity to know the case against one and answer it before a decision is reached. The other options describe Fusion of powers, Amendment, Secret ballot.
items.t: Rule of law and natural justice

items.q: Which term is described by “the lawful suspension or narrowing of guarantees during a declared emergency”?
o: Right to life
Fundamental rights
Right to property
Derogation
items.s: Derogation is the lawful suspension or narrowing of guarantees during a declared emergency.

items.q: Which term is described by “the guarantee that no person may be killed except in execution of a lawful sentence”?
o: Freedom of association
Personal liberty
Freedom of movement
Right to life
items.s: Right to life is the guarantee that no person may be killed except in execution of a lawful sentence.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Entrenchment?
o: the liberty to join with others in forming groups for lawful purposes
a judgment of a court of another country, persuasive in Nigeria but not binding
the protection of a provision by making its alteration harder than ordinary change
the approval of a change by a stated proportion of the component legislatures
items.s: Entrenchment: the protection of a provision by making its alteration harder than ordinary change. The other options describe Ratification by states, Foreign decision, Freedom of association.

items.q: Which term is described by “a body of rules spread across statutes, conventions and judicial decisions rather than gathered in one document”?
o: Constituent power
Written constitution
Unwritten constitution
Constitutionalism
items.s: Unwritten constitution is a body of rules spread across statutes, conventions and judicial decisions rather than gathered in one document.
items.t: Nature and forms of a constitution

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Confederation?
o: a lawmaking body with two houses that must both approve a bill before it passes
a loose union in which the component units keep final authority and the centre acts as their agent
a lawmaking body consisting of only one house
the method of voting in which no one can tell how another cast his vote
items.s: Confederation: a loose union in which the component units keep final authority and the centre acts as their agent. The other options describe Bicameral legislature, Unicameral legislature, Secret ballot.

items.q: Constituent power may be defined as
o: the subjects left to the component states alone, on which the centre has no power
the authority of a people to adopt or replace the fundamental document of their state
the power of the legislature to pass a measure despite a refusal of approval
the holding of membership of two states at the same time
items.s: Constituent power: the authority of a people to adopt or replace the fundamental document of their state. The other options describe Dual citizenship, Override, Residual matters.
items.t: Nature and forms of a constitution

items.q: Which of the following best describes Franchise?
o: the fair procedure that must be followed before life, liberty or property is taken away
the qualified entitlement to vote in public elections
the legal status of belonging to a state and enjoying its protection
the formal approval by the head of state that turns a passed bill into law
items.s: Franchise: the qualified entitlement to vote in public elections. The other options describe Due process, Assent, Citizenship.

items.q: The statement “the voluntary giving up of one's membership of a state” describes which of the following?
o: Renunciation
Citizenship by registration
Naturalisation
Citizenship by birth
items.s: Renunciation is the voluntary giving up of one's membership of a state.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Supremacy of the constitution.
o: the principle that no one may sit in judgment on a matter in which he has an interest
the order requiring a person holding another in custody to produce him and justify the detention
the principle that every other rule or act must give way to the fundamental document and be void if inconsistent
the holding of membership of two states at the same time
items.s: Supremacy of the constitution: the principle that every other rule or act must give way to the fundamental document and be void if inconsistent. The other options describe Dual citizenship, Nemo judex in causa sua, Habeas corpus.

items.q: Habeas corpus may be defined as
o: the published opinions of scholars, which courts may consult for guidance without being bound
the division of governmental authority among three distinct organs, each with its own function
the chief law officer of the state, who advises government and conducts prosecutions
the order requiring a person holding another in custody to produce him and justify the detention
items.s: Habeas corpus: the order requiring a person holding another in custody to produce him and justify the detention. The other options describe Writings of jurists, Separation of powers, Attorney General.
items.t: Rule of law and natural justice

items.q: Which term is described by “the position that every person, whatever his office, is answerable to the same ordinary courts”?
o: Arbitrary power
Rule of law
Equality before the law
Nemo judex in causa sua
items.s: Equality before the law is the position that every person, whatever his office, is answerable to the same ordinary courts.
items.t: Rule of law and natural justice

items.q: Citizenship by birth may be defined as
o: a structure in which one central government holds all authority and local bodies exist at its pleasure
the position that every person, whatever his office, is answerable to the same ordinary courts
the doctrine that an act beyond the limits of a conferred authority is void
the status acquired by being born to citizen parents, or in the country in stated cases
items.s: Citizenship by birth: the status acquired by being born to citizen parents, or in the country in stated cases. The other options describe Unitary system, Equality before the law, Ultra vires.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Due process.
o: the principle that both sides must be heard before a decision affecting them is taken
the fair procedure that must be followed before life, liberty or property is taken away
authority exercised at the mere will of its holder without any settled standard
the protection of a provision by making its alteration harder than ordinary change
items.s: Due process: the fair procedure that must be followed before life, liberty or property is taken away. The other options describe Entrenchment, Audi alteram partem, Arbitrary power.
items.t: Rule of law and natural justice

items.q: Which term is described by “the division of governmental authority among three distinct organs, each with its own function”?
o: Fusion of powers
Judiciary
Delegated legislation
Separation of powers
items.s: Separation of powers is the division of governmental authority among three distinct organs, each with its own function.

items.q: Bicameral legislature may be defined as
o: the presiding officer of the lower house, chosen by its members from among themselves
a structure in which one central government holds all authority and local bodies exist at its pleasure
the guarantee against deprivation of one's possessions except for public purposes with compensation
a lawmaking body with two houses that must both approve a bill before it passes
items.s: Bicameral legislature: a lawmaking body with two houses that must both approve a bill before it passes. The other options describe Unitary system, Speaker, Right to property.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Exclusive legislative list.
o: the subjects upon which only the central legislature may make rules
one that can be changed by the same ordinary process used for making statutes
the voluntary giving up of one's membership of a state
the fair procedure that must be followed before life, liberty or property is taken away
items.s: Exclusive legislative list: the subjects upon which only the central legislature may make rules. The other options describe Flexible constitution, Due process, Renunciation.

items.q: Which term is described by “the opening provision declaring the fundamental document binding on all authorities and persons”?
o: Grundnorm
Supremacy clause
Supremacy of the constitution
Ultra vires
items.s: Supremacy clause is the opening provision declaring the fundamental document binding on all authorities and persons.

items.q: Which term is described by “authority exercised at the mere will of its holder without any settled standard”?
o: Nemo judex in causa sua
Fair hearing
Arbitrary power
Habeas corpus
items.s: Arbitrary power is authority exercised at the mere will of its holder without any settled standard.
items.t: Rule of law and natural justice

items.q: Which of the following best describes Judicial review?
o: the organ that carries out policy and administers the state from day to day
the body of principles developed to soften the harshness of the strict old rules
the power of a court to examine an act of government and set it aside as unlawful
the liberty to go anywhere within the country and to leave and re-enter it
items.s: Judicial review: the power of a court to examine an act of government and set it aside as unlawful. The other options describe Equity, Executive, Freedom of movement.

items.q: Which term is described by “the liberty to go anywhere within the country and to leave and re-enter it”?
o: Freedom of expression
Freedom of movement
Right to property
Right to life
items.s: Freedom of movement is the liberty to go anywhere within the country and to leave and re-enter it.

items.q: Which term is described by “a lawmaking body consisting of only one house”?
o: Assent
Attorney General
Unicameral legislature
Override
items.s: Unicameral legislature is a lawmaking body consisting of only one house.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Flexible constitution?
o: the chief law officer of the state, who advises government and conducts prosecutions
the subjects left to the component states alone, on which the centre has no power
one that can be changed by the same ordinary process used for making statutes
rules derived from the accepted practices of a community and treated as binding within it
items.s: Flexible constitution: one that can be changed by the same ordinary process used for making statutes. The other options describe Customary law, Attorney General, Residual matters.
items.t: Nature and forms of a constitution

items.q: Unwritten constitution may be defined as
o: the order requiring a person holding another in custody to produce him and justify the detention
the power of the legislature to pass a measure despite a refusal of approval
a body of rules spread across statutes, conventions and judicial decisions rather than gathered in one document
the organ that settles disputes and applies the rules to concrete cases
items.s: Unwritten constitution: a body of rules spread across statutes, conventions and judicial decisions rather than gathered in one document. The other options describe Judiciary, Override, Habeas corpus.
items.t: Nature and forms of a constitution

items.q: The statement “the formal approval by the head of state that turns a passed bill into law” describes which of the following?
o: Attorney General
Veto
Assent
Override
items.s: Assent is the formal approval by the head of state that turns a passed bill into law.

items.q: Secret ballot may be defined as
o: a lawmaking body consisting of only one house
a structure in which one central government holds all authority and local bodies exist at its pleasure
the special regime declared in a grave crisis, allowing temporary extraordinary measures
the method of voting in which no one can tell how another cast his vote
items.s: Secret ballot: the method of voting in which no one can tell how another cast his vote. The other options describe State of emergency, Unicameral legislature, Unitary system.

items.q: The statement “a structure in which one central government holds all authority and local bodies exist at its pleasure” describes which of the following?
o: Confederation
Unitary system
Exclusive legislative list
Derivation
items.s: Unitary system is a structure in which one central government holds all authority and local bodies exist at its pleasure.

items.q: Common law is best described as
o: a rule laid down in an earlier decided case that later courts of the same level must follow
a judgment of a court of another country, persuasive in Nigeria but not binding

items.q: In this course, Derivation refers to
o: a loose union in which the component units keep final authority and the centre acts as their agent
the principle that a unit receives a share of revenue according to what is produced within its area
a system in which authority is shared between a central government and component units of one state
the subjects upon which only the central legislature may make rules
items.s: Derivation: the principle that a unit receives a share of revenue according to what is produced within its area. The other options describe Exclusive legislative list, Confederation, Federalism.

items.q: In this course, Fundamental rights refers to
o: the guarantees secured for every person and enforceable in court against the state
the lawful suspension or narrowing of guarantees during a declared emergency
the guarantee against deprivation of one's possessions except for public purposes with compensation
the freedom from arrest or detention except on grounds and by procedure allowed by law
items.s: Fundamental rights: the guarantees secured for every person and enforceable in court against the state. The other options describe Derogation, Personal liberty, Right to property.

items.q: “the route by which a foreigner married to a citizen may acquire the same status” is the definition of
o: Citizenship by birth
Citizenship by registration
Renunciation
Franchise
items.s: Citizenship by registration is the route by which a foreigner married to a citizen may acquire the same status.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Unicameral legislature?
o: the refusal of the head of state to approve a measure passed by the legislature
a lawmaking body consisting of only one house
the power of the legislature to pass a measure despite a refusal of approval
the head of the judicial arm, who presides over the highest court in the land
items.s: Unicameral legislature: a lawmaking body consisting of only one house. The other options describe Chief Justice, Override, Veto.

items.q: In this course, Freedom from discrimination refers to
o: the liberty to join with others in forming groups for lawful purposes
the freedom from arrest or detention except on grounds and by procedure allowed by law
the guarantee that no person may be killed except in execution of a lawful sentence
the guarantee that no one is treated worse because of ethnic group, sex, religion or birth
items.s: Freedom from discrimination: the guarantee that no one is treated worse because of ethnic group, sex, religion or birth. The other options describe Personal liberty, Freedom of association, Right to life.

items.q: In this course, Citizenship refers to
o: the route by which a foreigner married to a citizen may acquire the same status
the method of voting in which no one can tell how another cast his vote
the legal status of belonging to a state and enjoying its protection
the status acquired by being born to citizen parents, or in the country in stated cases
items.s: Citizenship: the legal status of belonging to a state and enjoying its protection. The other options describe Citizenship by birth, Secret ballot, Citizenship by registration.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the body of rules, written or unwritten, that establishes the organs of a state and limits their authority”
o: Constituent power
Constitutional convention
Constitution
Written constitution
items.s: Constitution is the body of rules, written or unwritten, that establishes the organs of a state and limits their authority.
